sentences.text: Struthiosaurus was a small armored dinosaur with size estimates ranging from 2 to 3 meters in length and weighing between 100 and 400 kilograms.
Geologist Eduard Suess first found a dinosaur tooth in 1859 at a coal mine near Wiener Neustadt, Austria.
The genus was formally named in 1870 or 1871 by Emanuel Bunzel based on a fragment consisting mainly of the posterior end of the skull and braincase.
Brain examinations suggest Struthiosaurus was sluggish and solitary, relying primarily on its armor to defend against predators.

Struthiosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia and is classified within the family Nodosauridae, where cladistic analyses suggest it is a basal member. In 1978, Walter Coombs classified it as a member of the Nodosauridae family, and it belongs to the subfamily Struthiosaurinae. Paleontologists recognize three valid species, including Struthiosaurus austriacus described by Bunzel in 1871 based on the holotype PIWU 2349/6.

Struthiosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Santonian to Maastrichtian stages, in regions including Austria, Romania, France, and possibly Hungary. It lived in Europe between 83 and 66 million years ago, with some records placing its range from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
There are 23 recorded fossil occurrences of Struthiosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
